items.title: Administrative Penalty System Non-Parking By-law - Housekeeping Amendments, CSD-2025-391

items.title: Policy - Live Streaming of Sports and Recreation Activities, CSD-2026-214
notes:
The Committee considered Corporate Services Department report CSD-2026-214, dated May 25, 2026 recommending that Council approve the Policy titled 'Live Streaming of Sports and Recreation Activities' attached to the report; and further, that staff be authorized to administer and update associated procedures, agreements, and requirements to ensure consistent, compliant and safe live streaming operations.

B. Cheyne was in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee.

notes: The Committee considered Infrastructure Services Department report INS-2026-231, dated May 8, 2026 recommending that an additional $290,000 be allocated from the Sanitary Capital Reserve to fund the design, contract administration, and construction of the additional works.

items.title: Delegated Authority - 'Restricted Acts' Provisions, COR-2026-182
notes: The Committee considered Corporate Services Department report COR-2026-182, dated April 4, 2026 recommending that in the event the provisions of Section 275 of the Municipal Act, as amended, come into force and effect between Nomination Day (August 21, 2026) and the end of the outgoing council’s term (November 14, 2026), the Chief Administrative Officer is granted authority to approve expenditures or other liabilities which are currently unbudgeted and with a value in excess of $50,000; and, that the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute agreements that have been approved by the Chief Administrative Officer during this period, subject to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor; and further, that any approvals granted by the Chief Administrative Officer during this period be reported to Council for information at the earliest opportunity following the Inaugural meeting of the new City Council.

attachments.name: 2026 Delegated Authority - Restricted Acts - COR-2026-182.pdf

items.title: Modernizing Human Resources Policies, COR-2026-207
notes:
The Committee considered Corporate Services Department report COR-2026-207, dated April 30, 2026 recommending that the modernized Human Resources policies, attached as Appendix A to the report be approved; and further, that the redundant Human Resources policies, attached as Appendix B to the report be repealed.

It was noted that any recommendation arising from this matter will be considered for ratification at the Special Council meeting later this date.

attachments.name: Modernizing HR Policies - COR-2026-207.pdf
COR-2026-207 Appendix A and B.pdf

items.title: Retrofit Affordable Housing Waterloo Region (RAHWR), DSD-2026-187
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-187, dated April 24, 2026 recommending that a one-time financial contribution in 2026 to Kitchener Housing Incorporated for the purposes of supporting the Kitchener Affordable Housing Retrofit Pilot Project be approved; and, that the General Manager of Development Services be authorized to execute a one-time grant agreement with Kitchener Housing Incorporated; said agreement to be to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor; and, that a financial contribution from the Affordable Housing operating account be approved in 2027 as a founding member contribution to the Retrofit Affordable Housing Waterloo Region (RAHWR) pilot program; and further, that the General Manager of Development Services be authorized to execute any documents or agreements pertaining to the City’s involvement in the RAHWR Pilot Program, provided however if such documentation requires any financial commitment that such expenditure either be accounted for within the budget or approved by Council; any said documentation to be to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor.

A. Marie Cipriani provided a presentation on this matter and responded to questions from the Committee.

E. Alani, Kitchener Housing Inc. and M. Day, WR Community Energy provided presentations outlining support for the proposed Kitchener Affordable Housing Retrofit Pilot.

A. Owodunni left the meeting at this time and re-entered.

items.title: Special Events Action Plan (2027-2030), DSD-2025-396
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-396, dated March 2, 2026 recommending that the Special Events Action Plan (2027-2030), attached as Attachment A of the report, be approved as the City of Kitchener’s guiding framework for the planning, delivery, and stewardship of special events; and, that staff be directed to apply the principles, event categories, and decision‑making frameworks outlined in the Action Plan when evaluating special event opportunities, within approved mandates and existing resources; and, that any requests for changes to service levels, staffing resources, funding models, or capital and operating budgets related to special events be brought forward for Council consideration through future issue papers and the annual budget process; and further, that staff be directed to develop an abbreviated action plan document that can be shared more broadly with stakeholders, including, but not limited to, the vision, principles and key actions of the Special Events Action Plan (2027-2030).

J. Dueck provided a presentation on this matter and responded to questions from the Committee.

S. Roth was also in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee. 

Councillor P. Singh left the meeting at this time and re-entered.

items.title: Arts and Creative Industries Action Plan, DSD-2026-061
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-061, dated March 2, 2026 recommending that Council receive and endorse the Arts & Creative Industries Action Plan (2027-2030), attached to the report as Attachment A, as the City of Kitchener’s guiding framework for clarifying the municipal role and establishing a defensible basis for prioritization related to arts and creative industries; and, that Council direct staff to apply the vision, guiding principles, areas of action, and decision‑making framework outlined in the Action Plan when evaluating arts and creative industries‑related opportunities, partnerships, and initiatives, within approved mandates and existing resources; and further, that any proposed changes to service levels, staffing resources, funding programs, or capital or operating budgets arising from implementation of the Action Plan be brought forward separately for Council consideration through future issue papers and the annual budget process.

A. Hallam provided a presentation on this matter and responded to questions from the Committee. 

J. Dueck and C. Bluhm were also in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee.
